subject: MAP & eval: HelixMed cost walk-through and timeline
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@helixmed.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixmed.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + MAP request: evaluation + cost model

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking a look — we're preparing for an evaluation of LLM-based clinical triage at HelixMed and would like Redwood to propose a mutual action plan (MAP) that includes a focused cost model. Key asks from our side:

- A MAP with milestone dates up to pilot completion (we need procurement and security sign-off by 2027-06-20).
- A unit-economics model showing tokens/$ under 3 scenarios (baseline, with prefix caching, with batching + caching). Please surface assumptions: avg prompt/response tokens, KV/prefix cache hit-rate, batching window and expected latency impact.
- An evaluation plan with acceptance criteria (p95 latency, throughput, quality regression tolerances).

Estimated volumes: ~150k prompts/day at peak; avg prompt 120 tokens in + 250 tokens out. SLA: p95 latency < 250ms preferred but we can accept up to 400ms during heavy traffic if cost delta is large.

Can your team share a short MAP draft and a ballpark cost breakdown by EOD Wednesday? We want to line up an internal budgeting conversation.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Product
HelixMed

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@helixmed.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + MAP request: evaluation + cost model

Jordan — thanks for the clear brief. Aditya will own the MAP deliverable and Marissa will pair on unit-econ scenarios; Karthik will validate the latency/throughput gating for the eval.

Attached is a lightweight MAP template (helixmed_map_draft_v1.xlsx) and a short runbook that shows how we model tokens/$ with caching and batching (token_econ_runbook.pdf). High-level plan below — we'll iterate on dates during the call:

1) Kickoff & data handoff — 2027-06-09 (security questionnaire, sample prompts, traffic shape)
2) Cost model draft (3 scenarios) — 2027-06-11
3) Eval environment & canary (week of 2027-06-14)
4) Pilot decision & procurement handoff — target 2027-06-20

Important assumptions we've started with (we'll confirm on call):
- Avg prompt in: 120 tokens; avg response: 250 tokens
- Baseline model cost: $12 / 1M output tokens (example number — we'll run model-specific pricing)
- KV/prefix cache: baseline 30% hit-rate; optimized 70% after prompt normalization
- Batching: 20–40ms batching window for small-latency apps; effective token saving depending on request concurrency

Next steps: can you confirm a 30-min slot tomorrow 06/08 at 10:00am PT for a joint MAP walkthrough? If that works we'll lock owners and align on the procurement checkpoint.

Thanks — Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@helixmed.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixmed.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + MAP request: evaluation + cost model

Grace / team — 10:00am PT works, thanks. A few clarifications to speed prep:

- Traffic shape: 150k prompts/day peak, with a weekday spike concentrated in a 10-hr window (avg 12k/hr peak).
- Prompt/response lengths: we see ~120 tokens in, ~250 tokens out on average; some longer cases go to 1200 tokens.
- Prefix reuse: many prompts share identical structured fields (patient triage metadata) — we estimate a 65–75% prefix reuse after some normalization on our side.
- Procurement: sign-off target 2027-06-20 but finance needs an internal review by 2027-06-15.

For the call we'll share a sample of anonymized prompts and a tiny synthetic traffic trace. Looking forward to the MAP draft.

Jordan

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & eval: HelixMed cost walk-through and timeline

Quick internal note after the walkthrough this morning — three scenario sketches (numbers are rounded and illustrative; we'll formalize in the MAP spreadsheet):

1) Baseline (no prefix cache normalization, conservative batching):
- Assumptions: 30% cache hit-rate, no effective batching (single-request windows)
- Tokens processed/day (outgoing) ~ 150k * 250 = 37.5M tokens
- Cost: at $12 / 1M out-tokens => ~$450 / day => ~$13.5k / month
- Effective tokens/$ = 83k tokens per $1

2) Optimized caching (prefix normalization applied):
- Assumptions: 70% cache hit-rate on prefixes, same model cost
- Effective live tokens/day = 30% of 37.5M = ~11.25M tokens
- Cost: ~$135 / day => ~$4.05k / month
- Effective tokens/$ = 277k tokens per $1

3) Batching + caching (20ms batching window, increased concurrency):
- Assumptions: same 70% cache hit-rate, batching reduces token overhead by ~8% (fewer repeated prompt tokens in requests), some p95 latency uplift (~30–50ms)
- Effective live tokens/day ~ 11.25M * 0.92 = ~10.35M tokens
- Cost: ~$124 / day => ~$3.7k / month
- Effective tokens/$ = ~302k tokens per $1

Notes / risks:
- Cache hit-rate is the biggest lever. Small normalization changes on HelixMed side yield big unit-econ wins.
- Batching helps the unit economics further but requires tolerance for small p95 latency increases and careful canarying.
- Need to validate model-specific per-token pricing (we used a placeholder $12 / 1M out-tokens). Also confirm how Redwood billing maps model variants and quantization profiles to price.

Action items:
- Marissa: convert these into the MAP spreadsheet and add a row for procurement review (due 2027-06-15).
- Karthik: run a quick latency simulation for the batching window at our target concurrency and share p95 estimates by 2027-06-10.
- Grace: confirm canary dates to align with HelixMed procurement window.

— Aditya
